questions: How much does a quest cost?
Are the quests paid?
Do I have to pay for a quest?
Is the quest free?
answer: It's free. There's nothing to buy or book: pick a quest in the catalog and head out for a walk.

questions: Is the site paid?
Is there a paid subscription?
What do I have to pay for on MeTravel?
answer: You don't have to pay: quests, articles, the map and the printable versions of quests are free. There is no subscription.

questions: Do I need to sign up?
Can I use the site without an account?
Do I have to register to read articles?
answer: You can read articles and browse the map and the quest catalog without signing up. A free account is needed to save routes, publish your own trips and continue a quest past the second task.

questions: Can I do a quest without signing up?
Do I need an account for a quest?
Why does the quest ask me to sign in after the second task?
answer: You can complete the first two tasks without an account. After that you need to sign in or sign up for free — that way your progress is saved.

questions: How do I sign up?
How do I create an account?
Can I sign in with Google?
answer: You can create an account with an email and password, or through Google, Apple or Facebook. It's free and takes less than a minute.

questions: What is a city quest?
What kind of quests does MeTravel have?
How does a city quest work?
answer: It's a walk around the city with tasks: you go from point to point, read short stories about the places and answer questions. The answers are right there on the street — on plaques, facades and monuments.

questions: How do I do a quest?
How do I start a quest?
Where do I begin?
answer: Open the quest on your phone and tap “Start quest”. At each point, read the story, complete the task and enter the answer, then move on to the next one.

questions: Do I need to book a quest in advance?
Is the quest run with a guide or in a group?
On which days do the quests take place?
Can I do a quest with a group of friends?
answer: There's no need to book: you do the quest on your own, from your own phone, on any day and at a time that suits you. A group can play from a single phone.

questions: Do I have to complete every point of the quest?
Can I skip a point?
Can I finish the quest early?
When does a quest count as completed?
answer: Points marked “Optional point” can be skipped, and the quest itself can be ended before the finale. It counts as completed if you have passed at least two thirds of the required points.

questions: How do I enter an answer in a quest?
Do capital letters and punctuation matter in the answer?
Should I write a number in digits or in words?
answer: Letter case, punctuation and “ё” instead of “е” don't matter. A number can be entered in digits or as a word.

questions: What if I can't answer a quest question?
Are there hints in the quest?
The quest won't accept my answer — how do I move on?
answer: Open the hint on the point card, if the task has one. After three wrong attempts you can skip the step and move on.

questions: Is my quest progress saved?
Can I continue a quest later?
Can I continue a quest on another phone?
answer: Yes. With an account your progress is saved and opens on any of your devices; without an account it is stored only on this device.

questions: Do I need internet during a quest?
Can I do a quest without internet?
Does the quest work offline?
How do I download a quest in advance?
answer: In the app you can download a quest in advance — the route, tasks and map will work without a connection. In a browser, save the quest and don't close the tab: after a page reload without a connection it may not open.

questions: Can I print a quest?
How do I do a quest without a phone?
Is there a printable version of the quest?
How much does a printed quest scenario cost?
answer: Any quest can be printed for free: open it in a browser and click “Print”. You'll get a quest book with a map, tasks, a diploma and a host page with answers — enough to walk the route without a phone.

questions: Are there quests for kids?
From what age can you do a quest?
Is a quest suitable for a 7-year-old?
answer: Yes, there are kids' quests for ages 5–7 and 8–10 and teen quests for ages 11–14. The age is shown on the quest card.

questions: Which cities have quests?
Are there quests in Minsk?
Where can I see the list of all quests?
answer: There are quests in Minsk and other cities of Belarus, as well as in a number of European cities. The full list by city and country is in the quest catalog.

questions: Does MeTravel have an app?
Where can I download the app?
Is there an Android app?
Is the app paid?
answer: Yes, the MeTravel app is available for iPhone, iPad and Android — on the App Store and Google Play. It's free.

questions: Is there an iPhone app?
Is the app on the App Store?
Does the app work on iPad?
answer: Yes, the MeTravel app is on the App Store for iPhone and iPad; it requires iOS 16.4 or later. It's free, with no in-app purchases.

questions: Why do I need the app if there's a website?
How is the app different from the website?
What can the MeTravel app do?
answer: The app has the same map, quests and guides as the website. On top of that, saved routes, articles, quests and map areas open without internet.

questions: How do I save a route to favorites?
Where can I find my saved routes?
How do I add an article to favorites?
answer: Tap the heart on the route card and it will go to your “I want to go” list. You need a free account for this, but the list will then be visible on all your devices.

questions: How do I add a route to my plan?
How do I mark that I've already been to a place?
What is “My calendar”?
answer: Open a travel page, tap “Add to plan” and choose a status: “I want to go”, “I'm planning” with a date, or “Was here”. All your marks are collected in the “My calendar” section.

questions: How do I plan a trip?
Does the site have a route planner?
How do I build my own route from points?
answer: In the “My trips” section, create a new trip and add points: from site search, by address or by clicking on the map. You need an account for this.

questions: Can I export a route to a navigation app?
How do I download a route as GPX?
Can I print a trip plan?
answer: From a trip plan the route can be downloaded as a GPX or KML file — you need at least two points with coordinates. On the website you can also print the plan.

questions: How do I add my own article?
How do I publish a trip on the site?
Can I write about my own trip?
answer: Sign in and choose “Add a trip”: fill in the description, route points and photos, then submit it for moderation. Once it has been reviewed, the article will appear on the site.

questions: What does an article need to be accepted for moderation?
Which fields are required in an article?
Why can't I submit my article for moderation?
answer: You need a title, a description of at least 50 characters, at least one route point, a country and a category. As long as something is missing, the article stays a draft.

questions: How long does moderation take?
When will my article be published?
How long does it take to review a trip?
answer: Moderation usually takes up to 24 hours.

questions: Can I save an article as a draft?
Who can see my draft?
Can I finish the article later?
answer: Yes. Only you can see a draft: you can keep adding to it and submit it for moderation when you're ready.

questions: What should I do if my article was rejected?
Why wasn't my article published?
Where can I see why publication was refused?
answer: In the “My travels” section the article will be marked “Rejected”, with the reason. Fix the issues and click “Correct and submit again”.

questions: Can I publish a short note instead of an article?
How can I share a trip quickly?
Do I have to write a long article?
answer: You don't have to: in the account menu, next to “Add a trip”, there is “Quick trip note”. All it takes is 1 to 10 photos, a place and a story of at least 50 characters; a note goes through moderation too.

questions: What's on the map?
How do I use the map?
Can I build a route on the map?
answer: The map brings together interesting places and travelers' routes. You can filter places by category and radius, and in route mode choose a means of transport and plot a path between two points.

questions: How do I filter places on the map?
How do I show only castles on the map?
How do I find places near me?
answer: Categories are chosen with the filters button, and the search radius with a separate button right on the map. If you allow geolocation, the map will show places near you.

questions: Where can I see a list of places?
How do I find sights by country?
How is the “Places” section different from the map?
answer: The “Places” section is a catalog of individual points: choose a country and a category, or use search. From its card, a place opens on the map or in the article that describes it.

questions: How do I find a route by country?
How do I search for articles and trips?
What filters are there in route search?
answer: The “Routes” section has search and filters: by country, category, transport, difficulty and month.

questions: What languages is the site available in?
How do I change the site language?
Is there an English version of the site?
Can I switch the site to Polish?
answer: The interface is available in Russian, Belarusian, Ukrainian, Polish and English. You change the language with the switcher in the site header, or on a phone in the “More” menu, under “Interface language”.

questions: What language are the quests in?
Are there quests in English or Polish?
Why did the quest open in Russian?
answer: Quests are being translated gradually. If there is no translation into the selected language yet, the quest opens in Russian with a note about the language.

questions: What language are the articles in?
Are articles translated into other languages?
Are there articles in English?
answer: Articles stay in the author's language — most often Russian. Only the site interface is translated.

questions: How can I contact you?
Where can I send a question or a suggestion?
How do I report a bug on the site?
answer: Write to us through the form on the contact page: enter your name, email and message.

questions: How do I report a mistake in a quest?
What if a quest point is no longer there?
The quest has a wrong answer — where do I report it?
answer: On the quest page, click “Report an inaccuracy”. If the point itself has changed, mark “This point has changed” on its card.

questions: How do I report an article or a comment?
How do I block a user?
What should I do if I see offensive content?
answer: Open the “Report, hide or block” menu next to the content or profile. Moderators review a report within 24 hours.

questions: What is MeTravel?
What is this site about?
What can I do on MeTravel?
answer: MeTravel is a website and app for independent travel: articles with routes and points on the map, a map of places and city quests. The content is written by travelers themselves.

questions: Do I need the app to play a quest?
Can I play a quest in the browser?
Do I have to install an app for a quest?
answer: No. A quest opens in your phone's browser — there is nothing to install. If you prefer, you can also play it in the MeTravel app.
